chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the Muhrim (one in Ihram) who catches game, making a Hady (sacrificial animal) obligatory upon him: he must slaughter it if he is performing Hajj in Mina where people slaughter, and if he is performing Umrah, he slaughters it in Mecca. And if he wishes, he may leave it until he returns and buys it, for his saying suffices. And if he wishes, he may leave it until he returns and buys it; this is a concession (rukhsah) in delaying the Fidyah (expiation) to Mecca or Mina. And the preferable course is to redeem it from where he caught it.

key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Expiation or ransom (compensation for a religious violation)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: Concession or dispensation in Islamic law
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca where sacrifices are made during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim slaughter the sacrificial animal if they catch game while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the geographical jurisdiction for offering the fidya (expiation) when game is caught during Ihram, distinguishing between the sanctity of Mina for Hajj and Mecca for Umrah. It highlights the juristic preference (afdal) for immediate slaughter at the site of capture to ensure prompt fulfillment of the obligation, while acknowledging the concession (rukhsa) to delay until reaching the respective holy cities. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the precise location of ritual acts within the boundaries of the Haram.
